source.original_text: For a real symmetric matrix A in a finite Euclidean space, restrict the Rayleigh objective to the unit sphere F(x)=xᵀAx and equip it with the induced metric. Its Riemannian gradient is the tangent projection of the quadratic ambient gradient2Ax, namely2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). The tangent projection of any ambient u is u−⟨x,u⟩x.

lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type u_1}
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (n : ℕ)
  [inst_3 : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] (A : E →L[ℝ] E),
  (↑A).IsSymmetric →
    ∀ (x : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)) (z : ↥(ℝ ∙ ↑x)ᗮ),
      (∀ (w : TangentSpace (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) x),
          ((d% fun y => inner ℝ (↑y) (A ↑y)) x) w = inner ℝ ((d% Subtype.val x) w) ↑z) ↔
        ↑z = 2 • (A ↑x - inner ℝ (↑x) (A ↑x) • ↑x)
decoder_context: Metric.sphere (0:E)1 consists of unit-norm vectors. (ℝ ∙ x)ᗮ is the real orthogonal complement of the span of x. Candidate subtype coercions map vectors into E.
E is a finite-dimensional real normed inner-product space. Fact(finrank ℝ E=n+1) supplies the sphere model dimension; 𝓡 n is its real n-dimensional manifold model.
A:E→L[ℝ]E is a continuous linear operator; A.IsSymmetric means inner(A v,w)=inner(v,A w) for all v,w.
TangentSpace I x is the abstract tangent type. mvfderiv I h x is the actual differential into a vector space, totalized to zero outside differentiability. ((↑):sphere0E1→E) is the literal inclusion.
Module.End.HasEigenvector A.toLinearMap μ x means Ax=μ•x and x≠0. The displayed objective is the literal quadratic restricted to the unit sphere.

The printed notation d% is mvfderiv for the inferred manifold model; modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) is the real n-dimensional model. Up arrows are subtype or continuous-linear-map coercions.

objects.original: A real symmetric matrix acting on a finite Euclidean space; the unit-sphere restriction of the quadratic Rayleigh objective.
objects.reconstructed: A symmetric continuous real linear operator on finite-dimensional real inner-product E; the literal restriction f(y)=inner(y,Ay) to the unit sphere.
objects.evidence: Original Example 3.36 at printed36/PDF52 specifies the symmetric matrix, the nonzero-vector quotient, its unit-sphere restriction, and the smooth quadratic extension. An orthonormal basis identifies this E/operator presentation with that source presentation; finite-dimensional linear maps are automatically continuous. The packet proves its ambient function equals the library quadratic instead of merely assigning it a name.

domains.original: The unit sphere in a finite real Euclidean space, with tangent vectors orthogonal to the chosen unit x and with the ambient-induced metric.
domains.reconstructed: E has real dimension n+1; x belongs to Metric.sphere 0 1; abstract tangent directions use the n-dimensional sphere manifold; ambient tangent representatives belong to (real span{x}) orthogonal.
domains.evidence: Original Example 3.36 at printed36/PDF52 and Example 3.62 at printed44/PDF60 identify the embedded tangent plane with x-perp. The source d-dimensional ambient space becomes n+1-dimensional E. The n=0 case is the legitimate two-point sphere in dimension one: its tangent plane is zero. A zero-dimensional ambient space has no unit x, so the indexed positive-dimensional presentation loses no nonempty source case.

quantifiers.original: For arbitrary real symmetric A and every unit vector x, test against every tangent direction; no existentially supplied differentiability, gradient witness or eigenvalue normalization.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible E,n,A and unit x, for every z in x-perp, the pairing identity for every abstract tangent w holds iff the ambient vector z equals 2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x).
quantifiers.evidence: Example 3.62 is a pointwise formula for every unit x, rather than a formula for a distinguished extremizer. The packet supplies the ambient quadratic gradient internally. Its binders impose no extra public differentiability identity or stationarity hypothesis.

assumptions.original: Finite real Euclidean ambient space, symmetric A, unit x, smooth quadratic restriction, and induced metric. No positivity or invertibility premise.
assumptions.reconstructed: FiniteDimensional real inner-product E, finrank E=n+1, A.IsSymmetric and x in the unit sphere; the literal quadratic restriction is used.
assumptions.evidence: The original smooth extension in Example 3.36 is polynomial. The packet constructs HasGradientAt with 2Ax, so smoothness is a consequence of its concrete objective and is not outsourced to an additional assumption. The sphere inclusion is smooth and its derivative identifies abstract tangents with the embedded tangent plane. Definitions 3.51-3.55 at printed41/PDF57 and Example 3.56 at printed42/PDF58 require the ambient-restricted metric. The packet uses the actual inclusion differential in that ambient pairing, which implements this metric instead of silently using a chart-space inner product.

constant_dependencies.original: The unscaled objective x-transpose A x gives ambient gradient 2Ax; the projection uses unit radius one. No dimension-dependent or spectrum-dependent constants.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The real coefficient is exactly 2, the sphere radius is 1, and the finrank index merely chooses the manifold model.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Example 3.36 printed36/PDF52 computes the two equal cross terms using symmetry; Example 3.62 printed44/PDF60 retains that coefficient. The packet adapter between natural-number two-fold addition and real scalar multiplication preserves 2. No one-half objective, nonunit radius, positive eigenvalue, or hidden dependence on n is introduced.

conclusion.original: The induced sphere gradient is the tangent projection of 2Ax, with formula 2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x); projecting any ambient u removes its radial component.
conclusion.reconstructed: A tangent candidate z represents the actual restricted differential through every inclusion-induced tangent pairing exactly when z=2(Ax-inner(x,Ax)x). The local proof also calculates the projector for every ambient u.
conclusion.evidence: Definition 3.58 and equation3.34 at printed42/PDF58 characterize the gradient by all tangent pairings; printed43/PDF59 explains projection under the induced metric. Example3.62/(3.40) at printed44/PDF60 supplies the unit radial-removal formula. The packet theorem uses this characterization rather than a named global gradient field. The code contains universal local hproj(u); hp applies it to 2Ax. Existence is not assumed: K.orthogonalProjectionOnto(2Ax) is already an element of K=x-perp, and hp identifies its ambient vector with the displayed G. Thus the universal iff does not hide an empty candidate space. Uniqueness follows because two such representatives have zero inner product against all x-perp directions, including their difference.

publication_context.current_lean_module:
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereGradient
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Rayleigh

/-!
# Rayleigh objectives on the unit sphere

Boumal Example 3.62: the induced gradient of the literal sphere restriction
of a symmetric quadratic is its projected ambient gradient. Critical points
are exactly unit eigenvectors. The pairing uses the actual sphere inclusion
differential; it does not replace the induced metric by a chart metric.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereRayleigh

open Metric InnerProductSpace
open scoped Manifold InnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

/-- The concrete Rayleigh vector is the unique ambient tangent representative
of the genuine sphere differential with the inclusion-induced pairing. -/
theorem sphere_rayleigh_characterization
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ,
      ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w =
          ⟪mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w, (z : E)⟫_ℝ) ↔
        (z : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E))) := by
  have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hg : HasGradientAt (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) (x : E) := by
    apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
    have hraw := (hA.hasStrictFDerivAt_reApplyInnerSelf (x : E)).hasFDerivAt
    have hfun : (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) = A.reApplyInnerSelf := by
      funext y
      simp [ContinuousLinearMap.reApplyInnerSelf_apply, real_inner_comm]
    have hlin : toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) =
        (2 : ℕ) • innerSL ℝ (A (x : E)) := by
      ext v
      simp [toDual_apply_apply, two_smul]
    rw [hfun, hlin]
    exact hraw
  let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ
  have hproj (u : E) : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto u : E) =
      u - ⟪(x : E), u⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    change (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.starProjection u = _
    rw [Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,
      Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton ℝ hx]
  have hp : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) : E) =
      (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
    rw [hproj]
    simp [inner_smul_right, smul_sub, smul_smul]
  intro z
  rw [SphereGradient.sphere_gradient_characterization n x hg z]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    exact (congrArg (fun v : K => (v : E)) hz).trans hp
  · intro hz
    apply Subtype.ext
    exact hz.trans hp.symm

/-- Genuine sphere stationarity is equivalent both to the Rayleigh-coefficient
equation and to actual eigenvectorhood; unit membership supplies nonzeroness. -/
theorem sphere_rayleigh_stationary_iff
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ∧
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      ∃ μ : ℝ, Module.End.HasEigenvector A.toLinearMap μ (x : E)) := by
  have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hxne : (x : E) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    simp [hz] at hx
  have hzero := sphere_rayleigh_characterization n A hA x 0
  have hd :
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
        A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    have he :
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
          ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
            mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0 := by
      constructor
      · intro h w
        rw [h]
        rfl
      · intro h
        ext w
        exact h w
    rw [he]
    have hs : (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) •
        (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ↔
          A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
      rw [eq_comm, smul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero]
      simp
    have hpair :
        (∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
          mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0) ↔
          (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
      simpa only [Submodule.coe_zero, inner_zero_right] using hzero
    exact hpair.trans hs
  refine ⟨hd, ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ,
      Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mpr (hd.mp h), hxne⟩
  · rintro ⟨μ, hμ⟩
    have hAx : A (x : E) = μ • (x : E) := hμ.apply_eq_smul
    have hcoef : ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ = μ := by
      rw [hAx, inner_smul_right]
      simp [hx]
    apply hd.mpr
    rw [hcoef]
    exact hAx

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereRayleigh

source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS-authored restatement of the sphere application and its two stationarity directions; no source text/PDF redistributed.

publication_context.statement: For a real symmetric matrix A, let F(x)=xᵀAx on the unit sphere with the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product. The chosen smooth ambient quadratic extension has gradient2Ax. The tangent projector sends u to u−⟨x,u⟩x, so the sphere gradient is2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). Its vanishing is equivalent to Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; thus the stationary unit vectors are exactly eigenvectors of A, and every unit eigenvector is stationary.

formulae.label: Unit tangent projector and gradient
formulae.tex: P_xu=u-\langle x,u\rangle x,\qquad \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).

formulae.label: Both directions of stationarity
formulae.tex: \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x\text{ is a unit eigenvector of }A.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, real symmetric matrix A and a unit vector x.
Unit sphere with the metric induced by the ambient inner product; F(x)=xᵀAx, the sphere restriction of the smooth quadratic extension.

obligations.label: Construct the actual restricted differential and its unique induced tangent representative, with explicit formula2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x).
Zero actual differential iff the Rayleigh-coefficient equation iff actual unit eigenvectorhood, including the converse.

lesson.title: Rayleigh objective: remove the radial part of 2Ax
lesson.statement: For a symmetric linear operator A on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, let F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ on the unit sphere. With its induced metric, the unique ambient tangent vector representing the genuine sphere differential is Gₓ=2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). More explicitly, every z in x⊥ represents that differential against every actual tangent direction exactly when z=Gₓ.
lesson.formula: \begin{gathered}F(x)=\langle x,Ax\rangle,\quad T_xS=x^\perp,\quad J_x=D\iota(x),\\ DF(x)[w]=\langle J_xw,z\rangle\ \forall w\ \Longleftrightarrow\ z=G_x\quad(z\in x^\perp),\\ G_x=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).\end{gathered}
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space of dimension n+1. In orthonormal coordinates A is the source real symmetric matrix; its continuous-linear-map representation adds no regularity assumption in finite dimension.
A is symmetric, not necessarily positive, positive definite or invertible. x has norm one. Nonzeroness of x and the Rayleigh eigenvalue identity are derived internally, not added hypotheses.

The objective is the literal sphere restriction F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ of the smooth quadratic q(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. The ambient quotient is defined only for y≠0; its equality with this restriction uses ‖x‖=1. No derivative of an off-domain totalized quotient is used.

The metric is the ambient-induced one. The actual inclusion derivative Jₓ maps abstract chart directions into x⊥. Pairings with Jₓw express this induced metric explicitly; no default chart inner product is identified with it.

n may be zero. The claims are pointwise, with every x and every tangent test direction quantified. They neither construct a global gradient-field object nor claim a convergence or extremal-eigenvalue theorem.

steps.title: Differentiate the symmetric quadratic
steps.text: Expand q(x+tv). Symmetry makes the two first-order cross terms equal, giving Dq(x)[v]=2⟨Ax,v⟩ and hence the genuine ambient gradient 2Ax. The implementation reuses Mathlib’s derivative, proves that its quadratic is literally q, and identifies its linear functional with the gradient dual. No gradient witness is supplied by the reader.

steps.title: Project onto the actual tangent plane
steps.text: Because x is a unit vector, the projection onto its normal line sends u to ⟨x,u⟩x. Subtracting this normal component gives the projection onto x⊥. Apply this to 2Ax and use bilinearity to obtain the displayed vector Gₓ. In particular Gₓ is tangent: ⟨x,Gₓ⟩=2(⟨x,Ax⟩−⟨x,Ax⟩‖x‖²)=0.
steps.formula: P_{x^\perp}u=u-\langle x,u\rangle x,\qquad P_{x^\perp}(2Ax)=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).

    change (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.starProjection u = _
    rw [Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,

  have hp : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) : E) =

    rw [hproj]
    simp [inner_smul_right, smul_sub, smul_smul]

steps.title: Use the induced differential characterization
steps.text: The existing genuine-sphere theorem applies to the actual ambient gradient just proved. The inclusion chain rule and its exact tangent range are already established in that parent: the restricted differential pairs with a tangent candidate precisely when it is the orthogonal projection. Replacing that projection by Gₓ gives the claimed formula and uniqueness. Existence uses the projected vector in x⊥, not an assumed solution.

reconstruction.text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed inner-product space of dimension n+1, where n is any natural number, and let A:E→E be a continuous real linear symmetric operator. Give the unit sphere S={x∈E:‖x‖=1} its n-dimensional sphere manifold structure. Define f:S→ℝ by f(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩ and let i:S→E be the inclusion. Write Df(x) and Di(x) for the manifold derivatives used by the Lean statement, with those derivatives totalized to zero outside differentiability. For every x∈S and every z∈(ℝx)⊥, the identity Df(x)[w]=⟨Di(x)[w],z⟩ for every abstract tangent vector w∈T_x S holds if and only if, as an equality of vectors in E, z=2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x).
